newsitem.title: UK: B.Midland, Lufthansa plan code-share flights.
newsitem.headline: B.Midland, Lufthansa plan code-share flights.

text.p: British Midland said talks with Deutsche Lufthansa AG are at "an advanced stage" on starting code sharing on additional passenger routes between the UK and Germany.
Code sharing involves selling a ticket for travel on one airline that can be used for completing the remainder of a journey on another airline.

Airline sources told Reuters that the routes in question are from the UK -- mainly using under-utilised Lufthansa traffic rights and airport slots at London Heathrow -- to Berlin, Dresden, Bremen, Duesseldorf, Hanover, Hamburg and Leipzig.
"It is true that talks are at an advanced stage to expand services between the UK and Germany on a joint basis," said a British Midland spokeswoman.
The two carriers started a joint Heathrow-Cologne-Bonn twice-daily service using British Midland Boeing 737 aircraft on April 24.
This service continues on from Cologne to Rome on a once-daily basis, also as a joint British Midland/Lufthansa venture.
Louise Shenton, British Midland's cargo marketing manager, said she was aware of the new joint venture route plans and the German destinations involved.
She said she looked forward to selling the available cargo capacity once the joint routes were inaugurated.
British Midland is 40 percent owned by Scandinavian carrier SAS.
